raw_response:
I will do it close to how I did last year, with small adjustments. On my 10.1 mu, fertilizer is a big cost, but losing yield costs more, so I will not cut too hard. Around here in Quzhou, for wheat-maize, most people still put the main money into nitrogen, keep phosphorus steady, and give some potassium if they want the stalks stronger and grain fuller. I have well irrigation, so I can push yield more safely than dryland. For wheat, I will keep improved seed, use rotary tillage after maize, put most phosphorus and potassium in as base fertilizer, then split nitrogen between base and topdressing. Wheat usually needs two or three waters here if the year is normal, and I will plan three because water is available and I do not want to risk poor grain filling. For maize after wheat harvest, I will use hybrid seed like most farmers here, because it yields better and stands better. I will do no-tillage or very light tillage after wheat if the machine can seed well, mainly to save time and labor, then give enough nitrogen because maize eats heavily. I will still keep some phosphorus and potassium in, not just urea, because if I only chase leaf color the ears do not always fill well. On pesticides, I will not spray blindly, but I will plan enough passes for weeds plus disease or insects when they show. This year I will aim for steady yield, not the cheapest plan.
